review.method: Encoded from the text of s.107. The offence needs three things at once — a suicide, abetment, and (for the enhanced tariff) a vulnerable victim — so the encoding is a small conjunction with a victim-category split. 'Mental illness' is undefined in the section and is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity rather than guessed.

in_scope: s.107(1) abetment of suicide (up to twelve years)
s.107(2) abetment of suicide of a child, person with mental illness, delirious or intoxicated person (death, life, or ten years minimum)
out_of_scope: ss.100-106 homicide and negligence (separate packs in.bns.homicide, in.bns.negligence)
s.108 attempt to murder (separate pack in.bns.attempt-murder)
abetment generally (BNS s.45: instigation, conspiracy, aiding)

sources.note: Assented 25 Dec 2023, in force 1 Jul 2024. India Code PDF.
Predecessor of s.107(1). The maximum rose from ten years (IPC) to twelve years (BNS); s.107(2) has no IPC equivalent.

facts.name: abetted
facts.label: The accused abetted the suicide (instigated, conspired, or aided)

facts.name: victim_category
facts.label: Category of the person who died by suicide

terms.definition: Instigates, conspires, or aids the suicide (BNS s.45). The encoding treats abetment as a single fact; which means of abetment is proved does not change the outcome.
A child, a person with mental illness, a delirious person, or an intoxicated person. Abetting their suicide carries the enhanced tariff in s.107(2).

branches.text: If any person abets the commission of suicide ...
branches.notes: No suicide means s.107 is not engaged. Abetting an attempt is not this offence.

branches.text: If any person abets the commission of suicide ...
branches.notes: A suicide without abetment is not this offence. The abetment is the whole offence.

branches.text: If any person abets the commission of suicide of a child or any person with mental illness or a delirious person or a person who is intoxicated
branches.notes: The enhanced tariff. This sub-section has no IPC equivalent.

branches.text: If any person abets the commission of suicide, he shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to twelve years, or with fine, or with both.
branches.notes: The general provision. The maximum rose from ten years (IPC s.306) to twelve years (BNS).

punishment_rules.text: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for not less than ten years, or fine, or both [s.107(2)]
Imprisonment up to twelve years, or fine, or both [s.107(1)]

ambiguities.question: What counts as 'mental illness' in s.107(2)?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: The enhanced tariff (death, life, or ten years minimum) turns on whether the victim had a mental illness. The section does not define the term, and the pack records only one reading, so the analyser reports n/a rather than a number.
ambiguities.position_a: Mental illness means a clinically recognised condition at the time of the suicide.
ambiguities.position_b: Mental illness includes any diagnosed or treated psychiatric condition, past or present.

variants.label: clinically recognised condition at the time (current encoding)

illustrations.text: Abetting an adult's suicide: s.107(1), up to twelve years.
Abetting a child's suicide: s.107(2), the enhanced tariff.

A suicide without abetment is not s.107.
Abetting an intoxicated person's suicide: s.107(2).
